title: Git
tagline: Version control from first commit to fixing a broken rebase.

artifacts.title: gitkit
artifacts.pitch: Your own Git sidekick: a command-line tool that refuses sloppy commit messages, stops secrets before they leave your laptop, and computes object ids exactly like Git does.
artifacts.summary: A .NET command-line tool with real Git hooks, assembled from the code you write in this track.
features: `gitkit lint-msg`: a commit-msg hook that enforces the 50/72 rules
`gitkit hash-object`: the same blob ids Git computes, from your own SHA-1 code
`gitkit scan`: a pre-commit hook that catches AWS keys, private keys and passwords
`gitkit install-hooks`: wire it into any repository in one command

out: commit message: subject ends with a period
1 possible secret(s). Remove them, or commit with --no-verify if you are sure.

artifacts.run: dotnet run -- help, then from any repository: dotnet run --project <this folder> -- install-hooks

Kit.cs: /// <summary>The commands. Each calls a piece you write in a lesson; until then it says which lesson builds it.</summary>
Console.WriteLine("gitkit: Git helpers you built in code-dojo");
Console.WriteLine("  gitkit lint-msg <file>       check a commit message (Git calls this as a commit-msg hook)");
Console.WriteLine("  gitkit hash-object <file>    print the blob id Git gives the file");
Console.WriteLine("  gitkit scan [paths...]       look for secrets in staged files, or in the paths given");
Console.WriteLine("  gitkit install-hooks         wire lint-msg and scan into this repository's .git/hooks");
// Git hands the hook a file that may hold comment lines; drop them like git commit does.
foreach (var p in problems) Console.Error.WriteLine($"commit message: {p}");
if (findings.Count > 0) Console.Error.WriteLine($"{findings.Count} possible secret(s). Remove them, or commit with --no-verify if you are sure.");
catch { return []; }   // no git on the PATH: nothing staged to scan
if (!Directory.Exists(".git")) { Console.Error.WriteLine("Run this from the top folder of a Git repository."); return 2; }

## Use it on a real repository
From the top folder of any Git repository:
dotnet run --project <path to this folder> -- install-hooks
From then on `git commit` refuses messages that break the rules, and stops when a staged file
looks like it holds a secret. `git commit --no-verify` skips the hooks when you really mean it.
